name: Smith & Nephew plc
sector: Healthcare / Medical Devices — Orthopaedics, Sports Medicine & ENT, Advanced Wound Management
moat_justification: Leading positions (#2 in sports medicine and advanced wound care, top 3-4 in orthopaedics) with brands, surgeon relationships and proprietary platforms (OXINIUM, CORI robotics, PICO NPWT), but larger rivals (Stryker, Zimmer Biomet, DePuy) hold stronger robotics ecosystems, hospital/GPO pricing power is high, gross margin has eroded from 74.0% (2019) to 68.0% (2025), and the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json ran only 7.1% / 5.6% / 4.9% / 7.0% / 8.1% over FY2021-25 — below or near the cost of capital through the cycle, with the company's own >10% ROIC target only a 2026 goal. A moderate 5/10, not a wide moat.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x2.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Smith & Nephew plc Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-03-16), registered American Depositary Shares class (Exhibit 2(d), Description of Securities); the company's FY2025 results announcement (2 March 2026) states a final dividend of 24.1 US cents per ordinary share (48.2 US cents per ADS) and its H1 2026 report an interim dividend of 15.6c per share (31.2c per ADS) — per-ADS amounts are exactly 2x per-share amounts; the company's shareholder resources page confirms a ratio change on 14 October 2014 to one ADS representing two Ordinary Shares) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 1.85 vs 3-yr median 1.29 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
one_liner: Diversified medtech with #2 positions in sports medicine and advanced wound care, moat 5/10 — Tier D: weighted IRR 7.5%, weighted IV@15% $11.42 vs $29.06 per ADS on the normalized median base ($1.29/ADS); even the super-bull IV@15% ($20.56) sits below the price, and the ADS clears 15% only at or below $11.42
moat_for: #2 global positions in sports medicine and advanced wound care; top 3-4 in orthopaedic reconstruction, sold in 100+ countries
Proprietary platforms and materials: OXINIUM implants, CORI handheld robotics, PICO single-use NPWT, ALLEVYN dressings, REGENETEN bioinductive implant
Surgeon training, clinical evidence and installed instrument sets create real switching friction in implants and arthroscopy
Diversified three-franchise portfolio (Orthopaedics, Sports Medicine & ENT, Advanced Wound Management) balances weakness in any one segment
moat_against: ROIC has not cleared the cost of capital through the cycle: roic_proxy 4.9-8.1% over FY2021-25 (fundamentals.json); company targets >10% only from 2026 and 12-13% by 2028
Gross margin erosion: 74.0% (2019) to 68.0% (2025) on pricing pressure, mix and China VBP
Bigger rivals' robotics ecosystems (Stryker Mako, Zimmer ROSA, DePuy VELYS) outscale CORI; US knee implants lost ground in 2026 (Q2 US knee revenue -7.2%)
High customer bargaining power: hospitals and GPOs demand proven cost-effectiveness; continuous innovation spend is required just to hold share
